title: Tuning, picks and the twelve-string guitar
summary: He tunes one way, uses thumb and finger, and played a twelve-string with three strings removed; also mentions Saints and old-time religion.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Do you ever tune the guitar different or is it always tuned one way?
I just tune it one way. I got the pick right in my pocket. Yeah. Oh yeah.

I see. Thumb pick and two finger picks. One finger pick. Like that. Yeah. Just two fingers. Thumb and a finger. Right. Thumb. Finger and a thumb. Oh. Right. Did you ever, do you play, have you always played on a six strings or have you ever played twelve string guitars? I've played twelve strings.
Have you had twelve strings guitar? Right.
You own one? Yeah. How long ago did you, when? I played on the air. On the tour, I looked up, on the air.

Larry Burndes had a twelve string guitar. You know. So, he had twelve strings on it and I took on nine strings. You took nine strings? Right. And left the rest of them in there. And I played with a finger and thumb. Finger and thumb.
You told, you said you played When the Saints Go Marching In. I don't know what that's right.
Right. When the Saints Go Marching In and then, the, the, the old time religion.
